Your account. Your league.

Saturday Club by 4th & Soul · Privacy and security

Saturday Club is an invitation-only college football pick’em league for fun. We store your league name, email address, account access, picks, game results, and standings across seasons so the league can operate.

Sign-in and invitations

Email/password accounts use a salted password hash. If you choose Google or Facebook, we use your provider’s account ID and email to create or connect your league account. Provider access tokens are used during sign-in and are not saved. You must have an invitation to create an account.

Invitation emails and commissioner-triggered weekly slate notices are sent through Amazon SES when configured. Slate notices go individually to active members using their league email address. You can turn slate notices off in your account’s Email preferences; the default is enabled. Delivery history records member IDs, attempts and status, and may be retained with league history. Text invitation buttons open your messaging app; you choose the recipient and send the message. Invitation links are single-use and expire in seven days. Do not forward an invitation intended for you.

League access

Your league name, results and standings are visible to league members. Other members cannot see your picks before games lock. After a published game reaches kickoff or is confirmed in progress, league members can see each member’s saved team selection and who has no saved pick, using league names. Commissioners manage access, invitations, games and results. We use essential session cookies to keep you signed in and short-lived cookies to protect social sign-in. Your browser may retain a pending invitation for the current tab.

How account information is protected

The production site uses HTTPS. League passwords are stored as salted scrypt hashes, and session tokens are hashed in the database. Sign-in cookies are marked Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite. Access checks run on the server, and new accounts require a valid invitation.

The AWS deployment is configured to encrypt its data disks and private S3 database backups. Local database files are restricted to their owner. Encryption at rest protects storage; authorized server operators can still access league data. These are implementation and deployment controls, not an independent security certification.

Password recovery

When email sending is configured, use Forgot password? on the sign-in form. We show the same response whether or not an email has an active account. Reset links contain random tokens, expire after 30 minutes and work once. Only token hashes are saved in the league database. The password changes only after a new one is submitted; existing sessions and other outstanding reset links are then revoked.

Reset links are kept out of server request URLs by using the link fragment, and the page removes that fragment after opening it. Never forward a reset email. Use a unique password or passphrase and a password manager. If a reset email was not requested by you, ignore it; it does not change your password.

External services

AWS hosts the service and sends configured invitation and reset emails. Google and Facebook handle their own sign-in when enabled. Your browser may request fonts from Google and team logos from ESPN, which receive technical request information such as your IP address. The application does not collect payment-card information.

Delete your account or provider connection

Contact your league commissioner through the person who invited you. Tell them the email associated with your Saturday Club account and whether you want to remove a Google/Facebook connection or delete the league account and its data. The commissioner can coordinate with the site operator to verify and complete the request. Deleting picks can change historical standings. Disabling an account revokes access but preserves history; it is separate from deletion.

You can also remove Saturday Club from your Google or Facebook account’s connected-app settings. This revokes provider access but does not by itself delete league data. Backups may retain deleted information until the backup retention period ends.
